notable_absence.finding: THE PAGE IS CALLED 'INDEX LIFECYCLE' AND NEVER NAMES A SINGLE INDEX STATE. The promoted `index-state` enum (scheduled for creation, deferred, building, pending, online, offline, abridged) is the corpus's model of exactly this page's subject, and the page does not mention any of its seven values - not even 'online', and not even 'deferred', despite having a paragraph about deferring a build. The promoted `indexer-node-state` enum (ready, pause, warmup, n mutations remaining) is likewise absent, as is the third, undefined Active/Warmup/Paused vocabulary that storage-modes.md uses. So on the question this round was asked to settle: THIS PAGE DOES NOT SETTLE THE STATE VOCABULARIES AND DOES NOT EVEN TOUCH THEM. It models the lifecycle as four activities (creation, building, updates, scans) with two internal phases, and the state enums model it as a set of labels; the two models are disjoint and no page in this batch joins them. That is a real documentation gap, not just an extraction gap: a reader who sees `"state": "deferred"` in system:indexes and comes to 'Index Lifecycle' to find out what that means will not find out. Also absent: any statement of where the build happens relative to the host node chosen in the creation phase, any mention of index replicas or partitions (index-replication.md's subject, though this page is the one that describes the build), and any `requiresEdition` or privilege statement.

cross_component_finding: TWO NAMES FOR ONE PARAMETER, IN ADJACENT BULLETS. The Index Scans section reads: '* If the index consistency is `not_bounded`, ...' followed immediately by '* If the scan consistency is `at_plus` or `request_plus`, ...'. Same parameter, two names, one bullet apart, and the reader is given no signal that they are the same thing. The registry promotes `n1ql:scan-consistency` and index-replication.md titles its section 'Index Consistency' with an anchor `#index-consistency` - which this very page links to as '[Index Consistency](index-replication.md#index-consistency)'. So 'index consistency' is a real term of art in this module, used as the section title on the neighbouring page, and here it is applied to one value of the parameter while 'scan consistency' is applied to two others. Second finding, on the same three lines: the enum is INCOMPLETE HERE. Four values exist (`not_bounded`, `at_plus`, `request_plus`, `statement_plus`) and index-replication.md lists all four; this page lists three and silently omits `statement_plus`. A reader who uses `statement_plus` gets no guidance from the page that explains what the scan coordinator does. Third: the page's architectural actors, 'the projector' and 'the indexer', appear only inside numbered step lists, are never defined, and are never linked to 'Index Service Architecture' (learn/services-and-indexes/services/index-service.md), which is where they are defined - and which, on that page, calls the projector part of a 'projector and router' pair that this page does not mention. Fourth, minor: step 4 of Index Building is the only step in either list written in the passive voice, so it is the only step that does not name its actor.
cross_product_finding: cloud/indexes/index-lifecycle.json (Capella) and server/7.2/learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/index-lifecycle.json (Server 7.2, under `learn/`) already cover this page, and the 7.2 one already minted `index:gsi-per-collection-scope` for the opening sentence - so the same fact has now been extracted three times from three trees, which is a genuine recurrence signal for phase 2. Two divergences worth recording: (a) the tree position moved between 7.2 (`learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/`) and 8.0 (`indexes/`), so version-to-version comparison of this page requires knowing about the move; (b) I minted `index-service:projector` and `index-service:indexer` here while server/8.0/learn/services-and-indexes/services/index-service.json holds `index-service:projector-and-router` for overlapping subject matter. Do not treat that as a duplicate to collapse blindly: one page describes a projector paired with a router, the other describes a projector feeding an indexer, and whether that is two names for one component or three components in a chain is a question the documentation does not answer on either page.
